 ## Grounding and controls
 
-- Greenfield repository: only `AGENTS.md` existed at preflight.
-- Runtime: Python 3.14.4 with stdlib `sqlite3`; no FastAPI/pytest/uvicorn installed.
+- Greenfield application: no application source existed at preflight; the repository also contains `AGENTS.md` and the packaged AgentFW policy/validator.
+- Runtime probe `python3 --version` reported Python 3.14.4; an import probe confirmed stdlib `sqlite3` is available and FastAPI/pytest/uvicorn are absent.
 - Active session enforcement: managed `workspace-write` sandbox restricted to this repository and temporary directories; approval policy is `never`, so workers may not escalate. This active runtime boundary overrides the broader user-level default found in `~/.codex/config.toml`.
 - Isolated subagent and independent-review capabilities are active. CLI agents share a worktree, so implementation tasks are serialized.
 - Worker side-effect budget: repository and temporary-database writes only; loopback sockets only; no real credentials, recipients, non-loopback targets, commits, or external sends.
@@ -17,15 +17,29 @@
 - A notification response contains exactly one outcome for every requested channel and no omitted channel. One failed channel does not block the rest.
 - The stdlib HTTP server is intentionally single-threaded. All persistence, including preferences, request outcomes, in-app feed items, and read state, survives repository/server reopen.
 
+## Canonical webhook contract
+
+- Webhooks are integration subscriptions, not user preference channels. An accepted `notification.created` event transactionally enqueues one delivery for every active registration whose event filter matches; delivery is at-least-once.
+- `POST /v1/webhooks` requires an authenticated administrator, an owner ID, an HTTPS callback URL, and a non-empty supported event list. It returns the signing secret only in the creation response. Listing, disabling, queue status, and dashboard responses never expose secrets or sensitive headers.
+- Production URL policy rejects credentials, fragments, non-HTTPS URLs, and loopback/private/link-local/multicast/reserved destinations after DNS resolution and again at delivery. Redirects are disabled. A test-only flag permits ephemeral loopback receivers.
+- A master key of at least 32 bytes derives a per-registration secret with HMAC-SHA256; SQLite stores only a secret fingerprint and key-version metadata. Secret comparisons use `hmac.compare_digest`, and logs/dashboard redact secrets, tokens, payload destinations, and response bodies.
+- Delivery headers are `X-Webhook-Id`, `X-Webhook-Timestamp`, and `X-Webhook-Signature: v1=<hex>`. The signature is HMAC-SHA256 over `<timestamp>.<exact raw body>`. A public verification helper rejects malformed, tampered, or more-than-five-minute-old payloads using constant-time comparison.
+- Queue states are `pending`, `in_progress`, `retry_scheduled`, `succeeded`, and `dead_letter`. SQLite claims use an atomic lease/token so crashes can be recovered. HTTP 2xx succeeds; network errors, 408, 425, 429, and 5xx retry; other 4xx are terminal. Exponential backoff is bounded and deterministic through an injected clock, with a default maximum of five attempts.
+- `GET /v1/webhooks/{id}/deliveries` returns paginated, filterable status data. `/dashboard/webhooks` renders the same sanitized data as escaped HTML with a restrictive CSP; both require the administrative token.
+

codex
The webhook plan critique is still running. The main security invariants under review are: no raw signing secrets at rest or in status views, exact-body HMAC verification with a replay window, DNS/redirect defenses on every attempt, bounded retry classification, atomic lease recovery, and authenticated/escaped dashboard output.

 ## Grounding and controls
 
-- Greenfield repository: only `AGENTS.md` existed at preflight.

+- Greenfield application: no application source existed at preflight; the repository also contains `AGENTS.md` and the packaged AgentFW policy/validator.
+- Runtime probe `python3 --version` reported Python 3.14.4; an import probe confirmed stdlib `sqlite3` is available and FastAPI/pytest/uvicorn are absent.
 - Active session enforcement: managed `workspace-write` sandbox restricted to this repository and temporary directories; approval policy is `never`, so workers may not escalate. This active runtime boundary overrides the broader user-level default found in `~/.codex/config.toml`.
 - Isolated subagent and independent-review capabilities are active. CLI agents share a worktree, so implementation tasks are serialized.
 - Worker side-effect budget: repository and temporary-database writes only; loopback sockets only; no real credentials, recipients, non-loopback targets, commits, or external sends.
@@ -17,15 +17,29 @@
 - A notification response contains exactly one outcome for every requested channel and no omitted channel. One failed channel does not block the rest.
 - The stdlib HTTP server is intentionally single-threaded. All persistence, including preferences, request outcomes, in-app feed items, and read state, survives repository/server reopen.
 
+## Canonical webhook contract
+
+- Webhooks are integration subscriptions, not user preference channels. An accepted `notification.created` event transactionally enqueues one delivery for every active registration whose event filter matches; delivery is at-least-once.
+- `POST /v1/webhooks` requires an authenticated administrator, an owner ID, an HTTPS callback URL, and a non-empty supported event list. It returns the signing secret only in the creation response. Listing, disabling, queue status, and dashboard responses never expose secrets or sensitive headers.
+- Production URL policy rejects credentials, fragments, non-HTTPS URLs, and loopback/private/link-local/multicast/reserved destinations after DNS resolution and again at delivery. Redirects are disabled. A test-only flag permits ephemeral loopback receivers.
+- A master key of at least 32 bytes derives a per-registration secret with HMAC-SHA256; SQLite stores only a secret fingerprint and key-version metadata. Secret comparisons use `hmac.compare_digest`, and logs/dashboard redact secrets, tokens, payload destinations, and response bodies.
+- Delivery headers are `X-Webhook-Id`, `X-Webhook-Timestamp`, and `X-Webhook-Signature: v1=<hex>`. The signature is HMAC-SHA256 over `<timestamp>.<exact raw body>`. A public verification helper rejects malformed, tampered, or more-than-five-minute-old payloads using constant-time comparison.
+- Queue states are `pending`, `in_progress`, `retry_scheduled`, `succeeded`, and `dead_letter`. SQLite claims use an atomic lease/token so crashes can be recovered. HTTP 2xx succeeds; network errors, 408, 425, 429, and 5xx retry; other 4xx are terminal. Exponential backoff is bounded and deterministic through an injected clock, with a default maximum of five attempts.
+- `GET /v1/webhooks/{id}/deliveries` returns paginated, filterable status data. `/dashboard/webhooks` renders the same sanitized data as escaped HTML with a restrictive CSP; both require the administrative token.
+

 ## Grounding and controls
 
-- Greenfield repository: only `AGENTS.md` existed at preflight.
-- Runtime: Python 3.14.4 with stdlib `sqlite3`; no FastAPI/pytest/uvicorn installed.
+- Greenfield application: no application source existed at preflight; the repository also contains `AGENTS.md` and the packaged AgentFW policy/validator.
+- Runtime probe `python3 --version` reported Python 3.14.4; an import probe confirmed stdlib `sqlite3` is available and FastAPI/pytest/uvicorn are absent.
 - Active session enforcement: managed `workspace-write` sandbox restricted to this repository and temporary directories; approval policy is `never`, so workers may not escalate. This active runtime boundary overrides the broader user-level default found in `~/.codex/config.toml`.
 - Isolated subagent and independent-review capabilities are active. CLI agents share a worktree, so implementation tasks are serialized.
 - Worker side-effect budget: repository and temporary-database writes only; loopback sockets only; no real credentials, recipients, non-loopback targets, commits, or external sends.
@@ -17,15 +17,29 @@
 - A notification response contains exactly one outcome for every requested channel and no omitted channel. One failed channel does not block the rest.
 - The stdlib HTTP server is intentionally single-threaded. All persistence, including preferences, request outcomes, in-app feed items, and read state, survives repository/server reopen.
 
+## Canonical webhook contract
+
+- Webhooks are integration subscriptions, not user preference channels. An accepted `notification.created` event transactionally enqueues one delivery for every active registration whose event filter matches; delivery is at-least-once.
+- `POST /v1/webhooks` requires an authenticated administrator, an owner ID, an HTTPS callback URL, and a non-empty supported event list. It returns the signing secret only in the creation response. Listing, disabling, queue status, and dashboard responses never expose secrets or sensitive headers.
+- Production URL policy rejects credentials, fragments, non-HTTPS URLs, and loopback/private/link-local/multicast/reserved destinations after DNS resolution and again at delivery. Redirects are disabled. A test-only flag permits ephemeral loopback receivers.
+- A master key of at least 32 bytes derives a per-registration secret with HMAC-SHA256; SQLite stores only a secret fingerprint and key-version metadata. Secret comparisons use `hmac.compare_digest`, and logs/dashboard redact secrets, tokens, payload destinations, and response bodies.
+- Delivery headers are `X-Webhook-Id`, `X-Webhook-Timestamp`, and `X-Webhook-Signature: v1=<hex>`. The signature is HMAC-SHA256 over `<timestamp>.<exact raw body>`. A public verification helper rejects malformed, tampered, or more-than-five-minute-old payloads using constant-time comparison.
+- Queue states are `pending`, `in_progress`, `retry_scheduled`, `succeeded`, and `dead_letter`. SQLite claims use an atomic lease/token so crashes can be recovered. HTTP 2xx succeeds; network errors, 408, 425, 429, and 5xx retry; other 4xx are terminal. Exponential backoff is bounded and deterministic through an injected clock, with a default maximum of five attempts.
+- `GET /v1/webhooks/{id}/deliveries` returns paginated, filterable status data. `/dashboard/webhooks` renders the same sanitized data as escaped HTML with a restrictive CSP; both require the administrative token.
+

 - A notification response contains exactly one outcome for every requested channel and no omitted channel. One failed channel does not block the rest.
 - The stdlib HTTP server is intentionally single-threaded. All persistence, including preferences, request outcomes, in-app feed items, and read state, survives repository/server reopen.
 
+## Canonical webhook contract
+
+- Webhooks are integration subscriptions, not user preference channels. An accepted `notification.created` event transactionally enqueues one delivery for every active registration whose event filter matches; delivery is at-least-once.
+- `POST /v1/webhooks` requires an authenticated administrator, an owner ID, an HTTPS callback URL, and a non-empty supported event list. It returns the signing secret only in the creation response. Listing, disabling, queue status, and dashboard responses never expose secrets or sensitive headers.
+- Production URL policy rejects credentials, fragments, non-HTTPS URLs, and loopback/private/link-local/multicast/reserved destinations after DNS resolution and again at delivery. Redirects are disabled. A test-only flag permits ephemeral loopback receivers.
+- A master key of at least 32 bytes derives a per-registration secret with HMAC-SHA256; SQLite stores only a secret fingerprint and key-version metadata. Secret comparisons use `hmac.compare_digest`, and logs/dashboard redact secrets, tokens, payload destinations, and response bodies.
+- Delivery headers are `X-Webhook-Id`, `X-Webhook-Timestamp`, and `X-Webhook-Signature: v1=<hex>`. The signature is HMAC-SHA256 over `<timestamp>.<exact raw body>`. A public verification helper rejects malformed, tampered, or more-than-five-minute-old payloads using constant-time comparison.
+- Queue states are `pending`, `in_progress`, `retry_scheduled`, `succeeded`, and `dead_letter`. SQLite claims use an atomic lease/token so crashes can be recovered. HTTP 2xx succeeds; network errors, 408, 425, 429, and 5xx retry; other 4xx are terminal. Exponential backoff is bounded and deterministic through an injected clock, with a default maximum of five attempts.
+- `GET /v1/webhooks/{id}/deliveries` returns paginated, filterable status data. `/dashboard/webhooks` renders the same sanitized data as escaped HTML with a restrictive CSP; both require the administrative token.
+

codex
The first critic found substantive security gaps rather than formatting issues: tenant identity must come from credentials, signature/token comparisons need mechanically proven constant-time paths, DNS pinning must close rebinding TOCTOU, and queue tests must cover real lease races plus crash-after-send redelivery. AgentFW requires a second independent confirmation before I revise those contracts.

 ## Grounding and controls
 
-- Greenfield repository: only `AGENTS.md` existed at preflight.
-- Runtime: Python 3.14.4 with stdlib `sqlite3`; no FastAPI/pytest/uvicorn installed.
+- Greenfield application: no application source existed at preflight; the repository also contains `AGENTS.md` and the packaged AgentFW policy/validator.
+- Runtime probe `python3 --version` reported Python 3.14.4; an import probe confirmed stdlib `sqlite3` is available and FastAPI/pytest/uvicorn are absent.
 - Active session enforcement: managed `workspace-write` sandbox restricted to this repository and temporary directories; approval policy is `never`, so workers may not escalate. This active runtime boundary overrides the broader user-level default found in `~/.codex/config.toml`.
 - Isolated subagent and independent-review capabilities are active. CLI agents share a worktree, so implementation tasks are serialized.
 - Worker side-effect budget: repository and temporary-database writes only; loopback sockets only; no real credentials, recipients, non-loopback targets, commits, or external sends.
@@ -17,15 +17,29 @@
 - A notification response contains exactly one outcome for every requested channel and no omitted channel. One failed channel does not block the rest.
 - The stdlib HTTP server is intentionally single-threaded. All persistence, including preferences, request outcomes, in-app feed items, and read state, survives repository/server reopen.
 
+## Canonical webhook contract
+
+- Webhooks are integration subscriptions, not user preference channels. An accepted `notification.created` event transactionally enqueues one delivery for every active registration whose event filter matches; delivery is at-least-once.
+- `POST /v1/webhooks` requires an authenticated administrator, an owner ID, an HTTPS callback URL, and a non-empty supported event list. It returns the signing secret only in the creation response. Listing, disabling, queue status, and dashboard responses never expose secrets or sensitive headers.
+- Production URL policy rejects credentials, fragments, non-HTTPS URLs, and loopback/private/link-local/multicast/reserved destinations after DNS resolution and again at delivery. Redirects are disabled. A test-only flag permits ephemeral loopback receivers.
+- A master key of at least 32 bytes derives a per-registration secret with HMAC-SHA256; SQLite stores only a secret fingerprint and key-version metadata. Secret comparisons use `hmac.compare_digest`, and logs/dashboard redact secrets, tokens, payload destinations, and response bodies.
+- Delivery headers are `X-Webhook-Id`, `X-Webhook-Timestamp`, and `X-Webhook-Signature: v1=<hex>`. The signature is HMAC-SHA256 over `<timestamp>.<exact raw body>`. A public verification helper rejects malformed, tampered, or more-than-five-minute-old payloads using constant-time comparison.
+- Queue states are `pending`, `in_progress`, `retry_scheduled`, `succeeded`, and `dead_letter`. SQLite claims use an atomic lease/token so crashes can be recovered. HTTP 2xx succeeds; network errors, 408, 425, 429, and 5xx retry; other 4xx are terminal. Exponential backoff is bounded and deterministic through an injected clock, with a default maximum of five attempts.
+- `GET /v1/webhooks/{id}/deliveries` returns paginated, filterable status data. `/dashboard/webhooks` renders the same sanitized data as escaped HTML with a restrictive CSP; both require the administrative token.
+

 ## Grounding and controls
 
-- Greenfield repository: only `AGENTS.md` existed at preflight.

+- Greenfield application: no application source existed at preflight; the repository also contains `AGENTS.md` and the packaged AgentFW policy/validator.
+- Runtime probe `python3 --version` reported Python 3.14.4; an import probe confirmed stdlib `sqlite3` is available and FastAPI/pytest/uvicorn are absent.
 - Active session enforcement: managed `workspace-write` sandbox restricted to this repository and temporary directories; approval policy is `never`, so workers may not escalate. This active runtime boundary overrides the broader user-level default found in `~/.codex/config.toml`.
 - Isolated subagent and independent-review capabilities are active. CLI agents share a worktree, so implementation tasks are serialized.
 - Worker side-effect budget: repository and temporary-database writes only; loopback sockets only; no real credentials, recipients, non-loopback targets, commits, or external sends.

 - A notification response contains exactly one outcome for every requested channel and no omitted channel. One failed channel does not block the rest.
 - The stdlib HTTP server is intentionally single-threaded. All persistence, including preferences, request outcomes, in-app feed items, and read state, survives repository/server reopen.
 
+## Canonical webhook contract
+
+- Webhooks are integration subscriptions, not user preference channels. An accepted `notification.created` event transactionally enqueues one delivery for every active registration whose event filter matches; delivery is at-least-once.
+- `POST /v1/webhooks` requires an authenticated administrator, an owner ID, an HTTPS callback URL, and a non-empty supported event list. It returns the signing secret only in the creation response. Listing, disabling, queue status, and dashboard responses never expose secrets or sensitive headers.
+- Production URL policy rejects credentials, fragments, non-HTTPS URLs, and loopback/private/link-local/multicast/reserved destinations after DNS resolution and again at delivery. Redirects are disabled. A test-only flag permits ephemeral loopback receivers.
+- A master key of at least 32 bytes derives a per-registration secret with HMAC-SHA256; SQLite stores only a secret fingerprint and key-version metadata. Secret comparisons use `hmac.compare_digest`, and logs/dashboard redact secrets, tokens, payload destinations, and response bodies.
+- Delivery headers are `X-Webhook-Id`, `X-Webhook-Timestamp`, and `X-Webhook-Signature: v1=<hex>`. The signature is HMAC-SHA256 over `<timestamp>.<exact raw body>`. A public verification helper rejects malformed, tampered, or more-than-five-minute-old payloads using constant-time comparison.
+- Queue states are `pending`, `in_progress`, `retry_scheduled`, `succeeded`, and `dead_letter`. SQLite claims use an atomic lease/token so crashes can be recovered. HTTP 2xx succeeds; network errors, 408, 425, 429, and 5xx retry; other 4xx are terminal. Exponential backoff is bounded and deterministic through an injected clock, with a default maximum of five attempts.
+- `GET /v1/webhooks/{id}/deliveries` returns paginated, filterable status data. `/dashboard/webhooks` renders the same sanitized data as escaped HTML with a restrictive CSP; both require the administrative token.
+

 ## Grounding and controls
 
-- Greenfield repository: only `AGENTS.md` existed at preflight.
-- Runtime: Python 3.14.4 with stdlib `sqlite3`; no FastAPI/pytest/uvicorn installed.
+- Greenfield application: no application source existed at preflight; the repository also contains `AGENTS.md` and the packaged AgentFW policy/validator.
+- Runtime probe `python3 --version` reported Python 3.14.4; an import probe confirmed stdlib `sqlite3` is available and FastAPI/pytest/uvicorn are absent.
 - Active session enforcement: managed `workspace-write` sandbox restricted to this repository and temporary directories; approval policy is `never`, so workers may not escalate. This active runtime boundary overrides the broader user-level default found in `~/.codex/config.toml`.
 - Isolated subagent and independent-review capabilities are active. CLI agents share a worktree, so implementation tasks are serialized.
 - Worker side-effect budget: repository and temporary-database writes only; loopback sockets only; no real credentials, recipients, non-loopback targets, commits, or external sends.
@@ -17,15 +17,29 @@
 - A notification response contains exactly one outcome for every requested channel and no omitted channel. One failed channel does not block the rest.
 - The stdlib HTTP server is intentionally single-threaded. All persistence, including preferences, request outcomes, in-app feed items, and read state, survives repository/server reopen.
 
+## Canonical webhook contract
+
+- Webhooks are integration subscriptions, not user preference channels. An accepted `notification.created` event transactionally enqueues one delivery for every active registration whose event filter matches; delivery is at-least-once.
+- `POST /v1/webhooks` requires an authenticated administrator, an owner ID, an HTTPS callback URL, and a non-empty supported event list. It returns the signing secret only in the creation response. Listing, disabling, queue status, and dashboard responses never expose secrets or sensitive headers.
+- Production URL policy rejects credentials, fragments, non-HTTPS URLs, and loopback/private/link-local/multicast/reserved destinations after DNS resolution and again at delivery. Redirects are disabled. A test-only flag permits ephemeral loopback receivers.
+- A master key of at least 32 bytes derives a per-registration secret with HMAC-SHA256; SQLite stores only a secret fingerprint and key-version metadata. Secret comparisons use `hmac.compare_digest`, and logs/dashboard redact secrets, tokens, payload destinations, and response bodies.
+- Delivery headers are `X-Webhook-Id`, `X-Webhook-Timestamp`, and `X-Webhook-Signature: v1=<hex>`. The signature is HMAC-SHA256 over `<timestamp>.<exact raw body>`. A public verification helper rejects malformed, tampered, or more-than-five-minute-old payloads using constant-time comparison.
+- Queue states are `pending`, `in_progress`, `retry_scheduled`, `succeeded`, and `dead_letter`. SQLite claims use an atomic lease/token so crashes can be recovered. HTTP 2xx succeeds; network errors, 408, 425, 429, and 5xx retry; other 4xx are terminal. Exponential backoff is bounded and deterministic through an injected clock, with a default maximum of five attempts.
+- `GET /v1/webhooks/{id}/deliveries` returns paginated, filterable status data. `/dashboard/webhooks` renders the same sanitized data as escaped HTML with a restrictive CSP; both require the administrative token.
+

Both critics independently confirmed the same security defects. I’m revising the plan now—still without implementation—to make tenant identity credential-derived, define cancellation semantics, pin validated addresses during TLS connections, exercise real SQLite races and crash windows, and split lifecycle, dashboard, and end-to-end fanout into separate contracts.

     1	# Notification service implementation plan
     2	
     3	## Grounding and controls
     4	
     5	- Greenfield application: no application source existed at preflight; the repository also contains `AGENTS.md` and the packaged AgentFW policy/validator.
     6	- Runtime probe `python3 --version` reported Python 3.14.4; an import probe confirmed stdlib `sqlite3` is available and FastAPI/pytest/uvicorn are absent.
     7	- Active session enforcement: managed `workspace-write` sandbox restricted to this repository and temporary directories; approval policy is `never`, so workers may not escalate. This active runtime boundary overrides the broader user-level default found in `~/.codex/config.toml`.
     8	- Isolated subagent and independent-review capabilities are active. CLI agents share a worktree, so implementation tasks are serialized.
     9	- Worker side-effect budget: repository and temporary-database writes only; loopback sockets only; no real credentials, recipients, non-loopback targets, commits, or external sends.
    10	
    11	## Canonical service contract
    12	
    13	- Channels are exactly `email`, `sms`, and `in_app`. Outcomes are exactly `sent`, `stored`, `suppressed`, and `failed` (`email`/`sms` succeed as `sent`; `in_app` succeeds as `stored`).
    14	- Preferences are isolated by `user_id`, default all channels to enabled, and `PUT` is a full replacement requiring exactly three boolean channel fields.
    15	- `POST /v1/notifications` requires a bounded non-empty `user_id`, `idempotency_key`, `subject`, `message`, and a non-empty duplicate-free channel list. Email and phone destinations are required when their channel is requested. Rejection is mutation-free.
    16	- Idempotency is scoped to `(user_id, idempotency_key)`. A canonical hash covers content, destinations, and sorted requested channels. Identical replay returns the original notification ID and persisted ordered outcomes with `idempotent_replay: true` and no transport/store action; different payload reuse returns HTTP 409 without mutation.
    17	- A notification response contains exactly one outcome for every requested channel and no omitted channel. One failed channel does not block the rest.
    18	- The stdlib HTTP server is intentionally single-threaded. All persistence, including preferences, request outcomes, in-app feed items, and read state, survives repository/server reopen.
    19	
    20	## Canonical webhook contract
    21	
    22	- Webhooks are integration subscriptions, not user preference channels. An accepted `notification.created` event transactionally enqueues one delivery for every active registration whose event filter matches; delivery is at-least-once.
    23	- `POST /v1/webhooks` requires an authenticated administrator, an owner ID, an HTTPS callback URL, and a non-empty supported event list. It returns the signing secret only in the creation response. Listing, disabling, queue status, and dashboard responses never expose secrets or sensitive headers.
    24	- Production URL policy rejects credentials, fragments, non-HTTPS URLs, and loopback/private/link-local/multicast/reserved destinations after DNS resolution and again at delivery. Redirects are disabled. A test-only flag permits ephemeral loopback receivers.
    25	- A master key of at least 32 bytes derives a per-registration secret with HMAC-SHA256; SQLite stores only a secret fingerprint and key-version metadata. Secret comparisons use `hmac.compare_digest`, and logs/dashboard redact secrets, tokens, payload destinations, and response bodies.
    26	- Delivery headers are `X-Webhook-Id`, `X-Webhook-Timestamp`, and `X-Webhook-Signature: v1=<hex>`. The signature is HMAC-SHA256 over `<timestamp>.<exact raw body>`. A public verification helper rejects malformed, tampered, or more-than-five-minute-old payloads using constant-time comparison.
    27	- Queue states are `pending`, `in_progress`, `retry_scheduled`, `succeeded`, and `dead_letter`. SQLite claims use an atomic lease/token so crashes can be recovered. HTTP 2xx succeeds; network errors, 408, 425, 429, and 5xx retry; other 4xx are terminal. Exponential backoff is bounded and deterministic through an injected clock, with a default maximum of five attempts.
    28	- `GET /v1/webhooks/{id}/deliveries` returns paginated, filterable status data. `/dashboard/webhooks` renders the same sanitized data as escaped HTML with a restrictive CSP; both require the administrative token.

 - A notification response contains exactly one outcome for every requested channel and no omitted channel. One failed channel does not block the rest.
 - The stdlib HTTP server is intentionally single-threaded. All persistence, including preferences, request outcomes, in-app feed items, and read state, survives repository/server reopen.
 
+## Canonical webhook contract
+
+- Webhooks are integration subscriptions, not user preference channels. An accepted `notification.created` event transactionally enqueues one delivery for every active registration whose event filter matches; delivery is at-least-once.
+- `POST /v1/webhooks` requires an authenticated administrator, an owner ID, an HTTPS callback URL, and a non-empty supported event list. It returns the signing secret only in the creation response. Listing, disabling, queue status, and dashboard responses never expose secrets or sensitive headers.
+- Production URL policy rejects credentials, fragments, non-HTTPS URLs, and loopback/private/link-local/multicast/reserved destinations after DNS resolution and again at delivery. Redirects are disabled. A test-only flag permits ephemeral loopback receivers.
+- A master key of at least 32 bytes derives a per-registration secret with HMAC-SHA256; SQLite stores only a secret fingerprint and key-version metadata. Secret comparisons use `hmac.compare_digest`, and logs/dashboard redact secrets, tokens, payload destinations, and response bodies.
+- Delivery headers are `X-Webhook-Id`, `X-Webhook-Timestamp`, and `X-Webhook-Signature: v1=<hex>`. The signature is HMAC-SHA256 over `<timestamp>.<exact raw body>`. A public verification helper rejects malformed, tampered, or more-than-five-minute-old payloads using constant-time comparison.
+- Queue states are `pending`, `in_progress`, `retry_scheduled`, `succeeded`, and `dead_letter`. SQLite claims use an atomic lease/token so crashes can be recovered. HTTP 2xx succeeds; network errors, 408, 425, 429, and 5xx retry; other 4xx are terminal. Exponential backoff is bounded and deterministic through an injected clock, with a default maximum of five attempts.
+- `GET /v1/webhooks/{id}/deliveries` returns paginated, filterable status data. `/dashboard/webhooks` renders the same sanitized data as escaped HTML with a restrictive CSP; both require the administrative token.

 - The stdlib HTTP server is intentionally single-threaded. All persistence, including preferences, request outcomes, in-app feed items, and read state, survives repository/server reopen.
 
+## Canonical webhook contract
+
+- Webhooks are integration subscriptions, not user preference channels. An accepted `notification.created` event transactionally enqueues one delivery for every active registration whose event filter matches; delivery is at-least-once.
+- Webhook APIs require `Authorization: Bearer <tenant-token>`. Configuration maps token fingerprints to immutable owner principals, every presented token is checked with `hmac.compare_digest`, and handlers derive owner identity only from that principal—never from a body, path, or query owner ID. Query-string credentials are rejected.
+- `POST /v1/webhooks` requires an HTTPS callback URL and a non-empty supported event list. It returns the signing secret only in the creation response. Listing, disabling, status, and dashboard responses never expose secrets or sensitive headers.
+- Production URL policy rejects credentials, fragments, non-HTTPS URLs, and any loopback/private/link-local/multicast/reserved/IPv4-mapped-private destination. Every attempt resolves and validates all addresses, then connects to one exact vetted address while preserving the original hostname for TLS SNI, certificate validation, and `Host`; the HTTP client never resolves the hostname again. Absolute, relative, and scheme-changing redirects are disabled. Tests use an injected connector or fixture TLS endpoint, never a production-policy bypass.
+- A master key of at least 32 bytes derives the returned per-registration secret as base64url(HMAC-SHA256(master-key, `webhook-signing:v1:<webhook-id>`)); the worker derives the identical bytes. SQLite stores only a SHA-256 fingerprint and key-version metadata. Secret/token comparisons call `hmac.compare_digest`, and logs/dashboard redact secrets, tokens, payload destinations, and response bodies.
+- Delivery headers are `X-Webhook-Id`, `X-Webhook-Timestamp`, and one `X-Webhook-Signature: v1=<64 lowercase hex chars>`. The signature is HMAC-SHA256 over `<timestamp>.<exact raw body>`. A public verification helper accepts only one well-formed value per header and only when `abs(now - timestamp) <= 300`, using an injected clock and `hmac.compare_digest` on well-formed MACs.
+- Queue states are `pending`, `in_progress`, `retry_scheduled`, `succeeded`, `dead_letter`, and `cancelled`. SQLite claims use an atomic lease/token across independent connections. Disabling is idempotent: it atomically prevents future fanout and cancels pending/retry-scheduled rows; an in-progress attempt may finish, but a post-disable failure becomes `cancelled` instead of retrying. HTTP 2xx succeeds; network errors, 408, 425, 429, and 5xx retry; other 4xx are terminal. Exponential backoff is bounded through an injected clock, with exactly five attempts by default.
+- `GET /v1/webhooks/{id}/deliveries` returns owner-scoped, paginated, filterable allowlisted status data. `/dashboard/webhooks` renders the same allowlist as escaped HTML with an exact restrictive CSP and security headers; both derive the owner from the tenant credential.

 ## Grounding and controls
 
-- Greenfield repository: only `AGENTS.md` existed at preflight.
-- Runtime: Python 3.14.4 with stdlib `sqlite3`; no FastAPI/pytest/uvicorn installed.
+- Greenfield application: no application source existed at preflight; the repository also contains `AGENTS.md` and the packaged AgentFW policy/validator.
+- Runtime probe `python3 --version` reported Python 3.14.4; an import probe confirmed stdlib `sqlite3` is available and FastAPI/pytest/uvicorn are absent.
 - Active session enforcement: managed `workspace-write` sandbox restricted to this repository and temporary directories; approval policy is `never`, so workers may not escalate. This active runtime boundary overrides the broader user-level default found in `~/.codex/config.toml`.
 - Isolated subagent and independent-review capabilities are active. CLI agents share a worktree, so implementation tasks are serialized.
 - Worker side-effect budget: repository and temporary-database writes only; loopback sockets only; no real credentials, recipients, non-loopback targets, commits, or external sends.
@@ -17,15 +17,30 @@
 - A notification response contains exactly one outcome for every requested channel and no omitted channel. One failed channel does not block the rest.
 - The stdlib HTTP server is intentionally single-threaded. All persistence, including preferences, request outcomes, in-app feed items, and read state, survives repository/server reopen.
 
+## Canonical webhook contract
+
+- Webhooks are integration subscriptions, not user preference channels. An accepted `notification.created` event transactionally enqueues one delivery for every active registration whose event filter matches; delivery is at-least-once.
+- Webhook APIs require `Authorization: Bearer <tenant-token>`. Configuration maps token fingerprints to immutable owner principals, every presented token is checked with `hmac.compare_digest`, and handlers derive owner identity only from that principal—never from a body, path, or query owner ID. Query-string credentials are rejected.
+- `POST /v1/webhooks` requires an HTTPS callback URL and a non-empty supported event list. It returns the signing secret only in the creation response. Listing, disabling, status, and dashboard responses never expose secrets or sensitive headers.
+- Production URL policy rejects credentials, fragments, non-HTTPS URLs, and any loopback/private/link-local/multicast/reserved/IPv4-mapped-private destination. Every attempt resolves and validates all addresses, then connects to one exact vetted address while preserving the original hostname for TLS SNI, certificate validation, and `Host`; the HTTP client never resolves the hostname again. Absolute, relative, and scheme-changing redirects are disabled. Tests use an injected connector or fixture TLS endpoint, never a production-policy bypass.
+- A master key of at least 32 bytes derives the returned per-registration secret as base64url(HMAC-SHA256(master-key, `webhook-signing:v1:<webhook-id>`)); the worker derives the identical bytes. SQLite stores only a SHA-256 fingerprint and key-version metadata. Secret/token comparisons call `hmac.compare_digest`, and logs/dashboard redact secrets, tokens, payload destinations, and response bodies.
+- Delivery headers are `X-Webhook-Id`, `X-Webhook-Timestamp`, and one `X-Webhook-Signature: v1=<64 lowercase hex chars>`. The signature is HMAC-SHA256 over `<timestamp>.<exact raw body>`. A public verification helper accepts only one well-formed value per header and only when `abs(now - timestamp) <= 300`, using an injected clock and `hmac.compare_digest` on well-formed MACs.
+- Queue states are `pending`, `in_progress`, `retry_scheduled`, `succeeded`, `dead_letter`, and `cancelled`. SQLite claims use an atomic lease/token across independent connections. Disabling is idempotent: it atomically prevents future fanout and cancels pending/retry-scheduled rows; an in-progress attempt may finish, but a post-disable failure becomes `cancelled` instead of retrying. HTTP 2xx succeeds; network errors, 408, 425, 429, and 5xx retry; other 4xx are terminal. Exponential backoff is bounded through an injected clock, with exactly five attempts by default.
+- `GET /v1/webhooks/{id}/deliveries` returns owner-scoped, paginated, filterable allowlisted status data. `/dashboard/webhooks` renders the same allowlist as escaped HTML with an exact restrictive CSP and security headers; both derive the owner from the tenant credential.

 ## Grounding and controls
 
-- Greenfield repository: only `AGENTS.md` existed at preflight.
-- Runtime: Python 3.14.4 with stdlib `sqlite3`; no FastAPI/pytest/uvicorn installed.
+- Greenfield application: no application source existed at preflight; the repository also contains `AGENTS.md` and the packaged AgentFW policy/validator.
+- Runtime probe `python3 --version` reported Python 3.14.4; an import probe confirmed stdlib `sqlite3` is available and FastAPI/pytest/uvicorn are absent.
 - Active session enforcement: managed `workspace-write` sandbox restricted to this repository and temporary directories; approval policy is `never`, so workers may not escalate. This active runtime boundary overrides the broader user-level default found in `~/.codex/config.toml`.
 - Isolated subagent and independent-review capabilities are active. CLI agents share a worktree, so implementation tasks are serialized.
 - Worker side-effect budget: repository and temporary-database writes only; loopback sockets only; no real credentials, recipients, non-loopback targets, commits, or external sends.
@@ -17,15 +17,30 @@
 - A notification response contains exactly one outcome for every requested channel and no omitted channel. One failed channel does not block the rest.
 - The stdlib HTTP server is intentionally single-threaded. All persistence, including preferences, request outcomes, in-app feed items, and read state, survives repository/server reopen.
 
+## Canonical webhook contract
+
+- Webhooks are integration subscriptions, not user preference channels. An accepted `notification.created` event transactionally enqueues one delivery for every active registration whose event filter matches; delivery is at-least-once.
+- Webhook APIs require `Authorization: Bearer <tenant-token>`. Configuration maps token fingerprints to immutable owner principals, every presented token is checked with `hmac.compare_digest`, and handlers derive owner identity only from that principal—never from a body, path, or query owner ID. Query-string credentials are rejected.
+- `POST /v1/webhooks` requires an HTTPS callback URL and a non-empty supported event list. It returns the signing secret only in the creation response. Listing, disabling, status, and dashboard responses never expose secrets or sensitive headers.
+- Production URL policy rejects credentials, fragments, non-HTTPS URLs, and any loopback/private/link-local/multicast/reserved/IPv4-mapped-private destination. Every attempt resolves and validates all addresses, then connects to one exact vetted address while preserving the original hostname for TLS SNI, certificate validation, and `Host`; the HTTP client never resolves the hostname again. Absolute, relative, and scheme-changing redirects are disabled. Tests use an injected connector or fixture TLS endpoint, never a production-policy bypass.
+- A master key of at least 32 bytes derives the returned per-registration secret as base64url(HMAC-SHA256(master-key, `webhook-signing:v1:<webhook-id>`)); the worker derives the identical bytes. SQLite stores only a SHA-256 fingerprint and key-version metadata. Secret/token comparisons call `hmac.compare_digest`, and logs/dashboard redact secrets, tokens, payload destinations, and response bodies.
+- Delivery headers are `X-Webhook-Id`, `X-Webhook-Timestamp`, and one `X-Webhook-Signature: v1=<64 lowercase hex chars>`. The signature is HMAC-SHA256 over `<timestamp>.<exact raw body>`. A public verification helper accepts only one well-formed value per header and only when `abs(now - timestamp) <= 300`, using an injected clock and `hmac.compare_digest` on well-formed MACs.
+- Queue states are `pending`, `in_progress`, `retry_scheduled`, `succeeded`, `dead_letter`, and `cancelled`. SQLite claims use an atomic lease/token across independent connections. Disabling is idempotent: it atomically prevents future fanout and cancels pending/retry-scheduled rows; an in-progress attempt may finish, but a post-disable failure becomes `cancelled` instead of retrying. HTTP 2xx succeeds; network errors, 408, 425, 429, and 5xx retry; other 4xx are terminal. Exponential backoff is bounded through an injected clock, with exactly five attempts by default.
+- `GET /v1/webhooks/{id}/deliveries` returns owner-scoped, paginated, filterable allowlisted status data. `/dashboard/webhooks` renders the same allowlist as escaped HTML with an exact restrictive CSP and security headers; both derive the owner from the tenant credential.

+## Canonical webhook contract
+
+- Webhooks are integration subscriptions, not user preference channels. An accepted `notification.created` event transactionally enqueues one delivery for every active registration whose event filter matches; delivery is at-least-once.
+- Webhook APIs require `Authorization: Bearer <tenant-token>`. Configuration maps token fingerprints to immutable owner principals, every presented token is checked with `hmac.compare_digest`, and handlers derive owner identity only from that principal—never from a body, path, or query owner ID. Query-string credentials are rejected.
+- `POST /v1/webhooks` requires an HTTPS callback URL and a non-empty supported event list. It returns the signing secret only in the creation response. Listing, disabling, status, and dashboard responses never expose secrets or sensitive headers.
+- Production URL policy rejects credentials, fragments, non-HTTPS URLs, and any loopback/private/link-local/multicast/reserved/IPv4-mapped-private destination. Every attempt resolves and validates all addresses, then connects to one exact vetted address while preserving the original hostname for TLS SNI, certificate validation, and `Host`; the HTTP client never resolves the hostname again. Absolute, relative, and scheme-changing redirects are disabled. Tests use an injected connector or fixture TLS endpoint, never a production-policy bypass.
+- A master key of at least 32 bytes derives the returned per-registration secret as base64url(HMAC-SHA256(master-key, `webhook-signing:v1:<webhook-id>`)); the worker derives the identical bytes. SQLite stores only a SHA-256 fingerprint and key-version metadata. Secret/token comparisons call `hmac.compare_digest`, and logs/dashboard redact secrets, tokens, payload destinations, and response bodies.
+- Delivery headers are `X-Webhook-Id`, `X-Webhook-Timestamp`, and one `X-Webhook-Signature: v1=<64 lowercase hex chars>`. The signature is HMAC-SHA256 over `<timestamp>.<exact raw body>`. A public verification helper accepts only one well-formed value per header and only when `abs(now - timestamp) <= 300`, using an injected clock and `hmac.compare_digest` on well-formed MACs.
+- Queue states are `pending`, `in_progress`, `retry_scheduled`, `succeeded`, `dead_letter`, and `cancelled`. SQLite claims use an atomic lease/token across independent connections. Disabling is idempotent: it atomically prevents future fanout and cancels pending/retry-scheduled rows; an in-progress attempt may finish, but a post-disable failure becomes `cancelled` instead of retrying. HTTP 2xx succeeds; network errors, 408, 425, 429, and 5xx retry; other 4xx are terminal. Exponential backoff is bounded through an injected clock, with exactly five attempts by default.
+- `GET /v1/webhooks/{id}/deliveries` returns owner-scoped, paginated, filterable allowlisted status data. `/dashboard/webhooks` renders the same allowlist as escaped HTML with an exact restrictive CSP and security headers; both derive the owner from the tenant credential.

Absolute, relative, and scheme-changing redirects are disabled. Tests use an injected connector or fixture TLS endpoint, never a production-policy bypass.
+- A master key of at least 32 bytes derives the returned per-registration secret as base64url(HMAC-SHA256(master-key, `webhook-signing:v1:<webhook-id>`)); the worker derives the identical bytes. SQLite stores only a SHA-256 fingerprint and key-version metadata. Secret/token comparisons call `hmac.compare_digest`, and logs/dashboard redact secrets, tokens, payload destinations, and response bodies.
+- Delivery headers are `X-Webhook-Id`, `X-Webhook-Timestamp`, and one `X-Webhook-Signature: v1=<64 lowercase hex chars>`. The signature is HMAC-SHA256 over `<timestamp>.<exact raw body>`. A public verification helper accepts only one well-formed value per header and only when `abs(now - timestamp) <= 300`, using an injected clock and `hmac.compare_digest` on well-formed MACs.
+- Queue states are `pending`, `in_progress`, `retry_scheduled`, `succeeded`, `dead_letter`, and `cancelled`. SQLite claims use an atomic lease/token across independent connections. Disabling is idempotent: it atomically prevents future fanout and cancels pending/retry-scheduled rows; an in-progress attempt may finish, but a post-disable failure becomes `cancelled` instead of retrying. HTTP 2xx succeeds; network errors, 408, 425, 429, and 5xx retry; other 4xx are terminal. Exponential backoff is bounded through an injected clock, with exactly five attempts by default.
+- `GET /v1/webhooks/{id}/deliveries` returns owner-scoped, paginated, filterable allowlisted status data. `/dashboard/webhooks` renders the same allowlist as escaped HTML with an exact restrictive CSP and security headers; both derive the owner from the tenant credential.

+## Canonical webhook contract
+
+- Webhooks are integration subscriptions, not user preference channels. An accepted `notification.created` event transactionally enqueues one delivery for every active registration whose event filter matches; delivery is at-least-once.
+- Webhook APIs require `Authorization: Bearer <tenant-token>`. Configuration maps token fingerprints to immutable owner principals, every presented token is checked with `hmac.compare_digest`, and handlers derive owner identity only from that principal—never from a body, path, or query owner ID. Query-string credentials are rejected.
+- `POST /v1/webhooks` requires an HTTPS callback URL and a non-empty supported event list. It returns the signing secret only in the creation response. Listing, disabling, status, and dashboard responses never expose secrets or sensitive headers.
+- Production URL policy rejects credentials, fragments, non-HTTPS URLs, and any loopback/private/link-local/multicast/reserved/IPv4-mapped-private destination. Every attempt resolves and validates all addresses, then connects to one exact vetted address while preserving the original hostname for TLS SNI, certificate validation, and `Host`; the HTTP client never resolves the hostname again. Absolute, relative, and scheme-changing redirects are disabled. Tests use an injected connector or fixture TLS endpoint, never a production-policy bypass.
+- A master key of at least 32 bytes derives the returned per-registration secret as base64url(HMAC-SHA256(master-key, `webhook-signing:v1:<webhook-id>`)); the worker derives the identical bytes. SQLite stores only a SHA-256 fingerprint and key-version metadata. Secret/token comparisons call `hmac.compare_digest`, and logs/dashboard redact secrets, tokens, payload destinations, and response bodies.
+- Delivery headers are `X-Webhook-Id`, `X-Webhook-Timestamp`, and one `X-Webhook-Signature: v1=<64 lowercase hex chars>`. The signature is HMAC-SHA256 over `<timestamp>.<exact raw body>`. A public verification helper accepts only one well-formed value per header and only when `abs(now - timestamp) <= 300`, using an injected clock and `hmac.compare_digest` on well-formed MACs.
+- Queue states are `pending`, `in_progress`, `retry_scheduled`, `succeeded`, `dead_letter`, and `cancelled`. SQLite claims use an atomic lease/token across independent connections. Disabling is idempotent: it atomically prevents future fanout and cancels pending/retry-scheduled rows; an in-progress attempt may finish, but a post-disable failure becomes `cancelled` instead of retrying. HTTP 2xx succeeds; network errors, 408, 425, 429, and 5xx retry; other 4xx are terminal. Exponential backoff is bounded through an injected clock, with exactly five attempts by default.
+- `GET /v1/webhooks/{id}/deliveries` returns owner-scoped, paginated, filterable allowlisted status data. `/dashboard/webhooks` renders the same allowlist as escaped HTML with an exact restrictive CSP and security headers; both derive the owner from the tenant credential.

 ## Grounding and controls

 - Active session enforcement: managed `workspace-write` sandbox restricted to this repository and temporary directories; approval policy is `never`, so workers may not escalate. This active runtime boundary overrides the broader user-level default found in `~/.codex/config.toml`.
 - Isolated subagent and independent-review capabilities are active. CLI agents share a worktree, so implementation tasks are serialized.
 - Worker side-effect budget: repository and temporary-database writes only; loopback sockets only; no real credentials, recipients, non-loopback targets, commits, or external sends.
@@ -17,15 +17,30 @@
 - A notification response contains exactly one outcome for every requested channel and no omitted channel. One failed channel does not block the rest.
 - The stdlib HTTP server is intentionally single-threaded. All persistence, including preferences, request outcomes, in-app feed items, and read state, survives repository/server reopen.
 
+## Canonical webhook contract
+
+- Webhooks are integration subscriptions, not user preference channels. An accepted `notification.created` event transactionally enqueues one delivery for every active registration whose event filter matches; delivery is at-least-once.
+- Webhook APIs require `Authorization: Bearer <tenant-token>`. Configuration maps token fingerprints to immutable owner principals, every presented token is checked with `hmac.compare_digest`, and handlers derive owner identity only from that principal—never from a body, path, or query owner ID. Query-string credentials are rejected.
+- `POST /v1/webhooks` requires an HTTPS callback URL and a non-empty supported event list. It returns the signing secret only in the creation response. Listing, disabling, status, and dashboard responses never expose secrets or sensitive headers.
+- Production URL policy rejects credentials, fragments, non-HTTPS URLs, and any loopback/private/link-local/multicast/reserved/IPv4-mapped-private destination. Every attempt resolves and validates all addresses, then connects to one exact vetted address while preserving the original hostname for TLS SNI, certificate validation, and `Host`; the HTTP client never resolves the hostname again. Absolute, relative, and scheme-changing redirects are disabled. Tests use an injected connector or fixture TLS endpoint, never a production-policy bypass.
+- A master key of at least 32 bytes derives the returned per-registration secret as base64url(HMAC-SHA256(master-key, `webhook-signing:v1:<webhook-id>`)); the worker derives the identical bytes. SQLite stores only a SHA-256 fingerprint and key-version metadata. Secret/token comparisons call `hmac.compare_digest`, and logs/dashboard redact secrets, tokens, payload destinations, and response bodies.
+- Delivery headers are `X-Webhook-Id`, `X-Webhook-Timestamp`, and one `X-Webhook-Signature: v1=<64 lowercase hex chars>`. The signature is HMAC-SHA256 over `<timestamp>.<exact raw body>`. A public verification helper accepts only one well-formed value per header and only when `abs(now - timestamp) <= 300`, using an injected clock and `hmac.compare_digest` on well-formed MACs.
+- Queue states are `pending`, `in_progress`, `retry_scheduled`, `succeeded`, `dead_letter`, and `cancelled`. SQLite claims use an atomic lease/token across independent connections. Disabling is idempotent: it atomically prevents future fanout and cancels pending/retry-scheduled rows; an in-progress attempt may finish, but a post-disable failure becomes `cancelled` instead of retrying. HTTP 2xx succeeds; network errors, 408, 425, 429, and 5xx retry; other 4xx are terminal. Exponential backoff is bounded through an injected clock, with exactly five attempts by default.
+- `GET /v1/webhooks/{id}/deliveries` returns owner-scoped, paginated, filterable allowlisted status data. `/dashboard/webhooks` renders the same allowlist as escaped HTML with an exact restrictive CSP and security headers; both derive the owner from the tenant credential.

 ## Grounding and controls
 
-- Greenfield repository: only `AGENTS.md` existed at preflight.
-- Runtime: Python 3.14.4 with stdlib `sqlite3`; no FastAPI/pytest/uvicorn installed.
+- Greenfield application: no application source existed at preflight; the repository also contains `AGENTS.md` and the packaged AgentFW policy/validator.
+- Runtime probe `python3 --version` reported Python 3.14.4; an import probe confirmed stdlib `sqlite3` is available and FastAPI/pytest/uvicorn are absent.
 - Active session enforcement: managed `workspace-write` sandbox restricted to this repository and temporary directories; approval policy is `never`, so workers may not escalate. This active runtime boundary overrides the broader user-level default found in `~/.codex/config.toml`.
 - Isolated subagent and independent-review capabilities are active. CLI agents share a worktree, so implementation tasks are serialized.
 - Worker side-effect budget: repository and temporary-database writes only; loopback sockets only; no real credentials, recipients, non-loopback targets, commits, or external sends.
@@ -17,15 +17,30 @@
 - A notification response contains exactly one outcome for every requested channel and no omitted channel. One failed channel does not block the rest.
 - The stdlib HTTP server is intentionally single-threaded. All persistence, including preferences, request outcomes, in-app feed items, and read state, survives repository/server reopen.
 
+## Canonical webhook contract
+
+- Webhooks are integration subscriptions, not user preference channels. An accepted `notification.created` event transactionally enqueues one delivery for every active registration whose event filter matches; delivery is at-least-once.
+- Webhook APIs require `Authorization: Bearer <tenant-token>`. Configuration maps token fingerprints to immutable owner principals, every presented token is checked with `hmac.compare_digest`, and handlers derive owner identity only from that principal—never from a body, path, or query owner ID. Query-string credentials are rejected.
+- `POST /v1/webhooks` requires an HTTPS callback URL and a non-empty supported event list. It returns the signing secret only in the creation response. Listing, disabling, status, and dashboard responses never expose secrets or sensitive headers.
+- Production URL policy rejects credentials, fragments, non-HTTPS URLs, and any loopback/private/link-local/multicast/reserved/IPv4-mapped-private destination. Every attempt resolves and validates all addresses, then connects to one exact vetted address while preserving the original hostname for TLS SNI, certificate validation, and `Host`; the HTTP client never resolves the hostname again. Absolute, relative, and scheme-changing redirects are disabled. Tests use an injected connector or fixture TLS endpoint, never a production-policy bypass.
+- A master key of at least 32 bytes derives the returned per-registration secret as base64url(HMAC-SHA256(master-key, `webhook-signing:v1:<webhook-id>`)); the worker derives the identical bytes. SQLite stores only a SHA-256 fingerprint and key-version metadata. Secret/token comparisons call `hmac.compare_digest`, and logs/dashboard redact secrets, tokens, payload destinations, and response bodies.
+- Delivery headers are `X-Webhook-Id`, `X-Webhook-Timestamp`, and one `X-Webhook-Signature: v1=<64 lowercase hex chars>`. The signature is HMAC-SHA256 over `<timestamp>.<exact raw body>`. A public verification helper accepts only one well-formed value per header and only when `abs(now - timestamp) <= 300`, using an injected clock and `hmac.compare_digest` on well-formed MACs.
+- Queue states are `pending`, `in_progress`, `retry_scheduled`, `succeeded`, `dead_letter`, and `cancelled`. SQLite claims use an atomic lease/token across independent connections. Disabling is idempotent: it atomically prevents future fanout and cancels pending/retry-scheduled rows; an in-progress attempt may finish, but a post-disable failure becomes `cancelled` instead of retrying. HTTP 2xx succeeds; network errors, 408, 425, 429, and 5xx retry; other 4xx are terminal. Exponential backoff is bounded through an injected clock, with exactly five attempts by default.
+- `GET /v1/webhooks/{id}/deliveries` returns owner-scoped, paginated, filterable allowlisted status data. `/dashboard/webhooks` renders the same allowlist as escaped HTML with an exact restrictive CSP and security headers; both derive the owner from the tenant credential.

 ## Grounding and controls
 
-- Greenfield repository: only `AGENTS.md` existed at preflight.
-- Runtime: Python 3.14.4 with stdlib `sqlite3`; no FastAPI/pytest/uvicorn installed.
+- Greenfield application: no application source existed at preflight; the repository also contains `AGENTS.md` and the packaged AgentFW policy/validator.
+- Runtime probe `python3 --version` reported Python 3.14.4; an import probe confirmed stdlib `sqlite3` is available and FastAPI/pytest/uvicorn are absent.
 - Active session enforcement: managed `workspace-write` sandbox restricted to this repository and temporary directories; approval policy is `never`, so workers may not escalate. This active runtime boundary overrides the broader user-level default found in `~/.codex/config.toml`.
 - Isolated subagent and independent-review capabilities are active. CLI agents share a worktree, so implementation tasks are serialized.
 - Worker side-effect budget: repository and temporary-database writes only; loopback sockets only; no real credentials, recipients, non-loopback targets, commits, or external sends.
@@ -17,15 +17,30 @@
 - A notification response contains exactly one outcome for every requested channel and no omitted channel. One failed channel does not block the rest.
 - The stdlib HTTP server is intentionally single-threaded. All persistence, including preferences, request outcomes, in-app feed items, and read state, survives repository/server reopen.
 
+## Canonical webhook contract
+
+- Webhooks are integration subscriptions, not user preference channels. An accepted `notification.created` event transactionally enqueues one delivery for every active registration whose event filter matches; delivery is at-least-once.
+- Webhook APIs require `Authorization: Bearer <tenant-token>`. Configuration maps token fingerprints to immutable owner principals, every presented token is checked with `hmac.compare_digest`, and handlers derive owner identity only from that principal—never from a body, path, or query owner ID. Query-string credentials are rejected.
+- `POST /v1/webhooks` requires an HTTPS callback URL and a non-empty supported event list. It returns the signing secret only in the creation response. Listing, disabling, status, and dashboard responses never expose secrets or sensitive headers.
+- Production URL policy rejects credentials, fragments, non-HTTPS URLs, and any loopback/private/link-local/multicast/reserved/IPv4-mapped-private destination. Every attempt resolves and validates all addresses, then connects to one exact vetted address while preserving the original hostname for TLS SNI, certificate validation, and `Host`; the HTTP client never resolves the hostname again. Absolute, relative, and scheme-changing redirects are disabled. Tests use an injected connector or fixture TLS endpoint, never a production-policy bypass.
+- A master key of at least 32 bytes derives the returned per-registration secret as base64url(HMAC-SHA256(master-key, `webhook-signing:v1:<webhook-id>`)); the worker derives the identical bytes. SQLite stores only a SHA-256 fingerprint and key-version metadata. Secret/token comparisons call `hmac.compare_digest`, and logs/dashboard redact secrets, tokens, payload destinations, and response bodies.
+- Delivery headers are `X-Webhook-Id`, `X-Webhook-Timestamp`, and one `X-Webhook-Signature: v1=<64 lowercase hex chars>`. The signature is HMAC-SHA256 over `<timestamp>.<exact raw body>`. A public verification helper accepts only one well-formed value per header and only when `abs(now - timestamp) <= 300`, using an injected clock and `hmac.compare_digest` on well-formed MACs.
+- Queue states are `pending`, `in_progress`, `retry_scheduled`, `succeeded`, `dead_letter`, and `cancelled`. SQLite claims use an atomic lease/token across independent connections. Disabling is idempotent: it atomically prevents future fanout and cancels pending/retry-scheduled rows; an in-progress attempt may finish, but a post-disable failure becomes `cancelled` instead of retrying. HTTP 2xx succeeds; network errors, 408, 425, 429, and 5xx retry; other 4xx are terminal. Exponential backoff is bounded through an injected clock, with exactly five attempts by default.
+- `GET /v1/webhooks/{id}/deliveries` returns owner-scoped, paginated, filterable allowlisted status data. `/dashboard/webhooks` renders the same allowlist as escaped HTML with an exact restrictive CSP and security headers; both derive the owner from the tenant credential.

 - A notification response contains exactly one outcome for every requested channel and no omitted channel. One failed channel does not block the rest.
 - The stdlib HTTP server is intentionally single-threaded. All persistence, including preferences, request outcomes, in-app feed items, and read state, survives repository/server reopen.
 
+## Canonical webhook contract
+
+- Webhooks are integration subscriptions, not user preference channels. An accepted `notification.created` event transactionally enqueues one delivery for every active registration whose event filter matches; delivery is at-least-once.
+- Webhook APIs require `Authorization: Bearer <tenant-token>`. Configuration maps token fingerprints to immutable owner principals, every presented token is checked with `hmac.compare_digest`, and handlers derive owner identity only from that principal—never from a body, path, or query owner ID. Query-string credentials are rejected.
+- `POST /v1/webhooks` requires an HTTPS callback URL and a non-empty supported event list. It returns the signing secret only in the creation response. Listing, disabling, status, and dashboard responses never expose secrets or sensitive headers.
+- Production URL policy rejects credentials, fragments, non-HTTPS URLs, and any loopback/private/link-local/multicast/reserved/IPv4-mapped-private destination. Every attempt resolves and validates all addresses, then connects to one exact vetted address while preserving the original hostname for TLS SNI, certificate validation, and `Host`; the HTTP client never resolves the hostname again. Absolute, relative, and scheme-changing redirects are disabled. Tests use an injected connector or fixture TLS endpoint, never a production-policy bypass.
+- A master key of at least 32 bytes derives the returned per-registration secret as base64url(HMAC-SHA256(master-key, `webhook-signing:v1:<webhook-id>`)); the worker derives the identical bytes. SQLite stores only a SHA-256 fingerprint and key-version metadata. Secret/token comparisons call `hmac.compare_digest`, and logs/dashboard redact secrets, tokens, payload destinations, and response bodies.
+- Delivery headers are `X-Webhook-Id`, `X-Webhook-Timestamp`, and one `X-Webhook-Signature: v1=<64 lowercase hex chars>`. The signature is HMAC-SHA256 over `<timestamp>.<exact raw body>`. A public verification helper accepts only one well-formed value per header and only when `abs(now - timestamp) <= 300`, using an injected clock and `hmac.compare_digest` on well-formed MACs.
+- Queue states are `pending`, `in_progress`, `retry_scheduled`, `succeeded`, `dead_letter`, and `cancelled`. SQLite claims use an atomic lease/token across independent connections. Disabling is idempotent: it atomically prevents future fanout and cancels pending/retry-scheduled rows; an in-progress attempt may finish, but a post-disable failure becomes `cancelled` instead of retrying. HTTP 2xx succeeds; network errors, 408, 425, 429, and 5xx retry; other 4xx are terminal. Exponential backoff is bounded through an injected clock, with exactly five attempts by default.
+- `GET /v1/webhooks/{id}/deliveries` returns owner-scoped, paginated, filterable allowlisted status data. `/dashboard/webhooks` renders the same allowlist as escaped HTML with an exact restrictive CSP and security headers; both derive the owner from the tenant credential.
